summary: Case-002 involves prof.kaya@aegean.edu. F2 shows IP 193.140.10.21 password-sprayed 54 accounts (60 failures) then authenticated as the user (T1110.003, T1078). F1 indicates impossible travel Manisa→Lisbon in 32 min (T1078.004). F3 notes VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) is CISA KEV-listed with multiple CVEs (T1133, T1190). Risk Gate directs escalation: sign-in path touches an exposed asset with compromise signals but no confirmed abuse chain. Confidence 0.6.

findings.claim: Impossible travel: Manisa → Lisbon in 32 min
Password spray then success: 193.140.10.21 failed against 54 accounts (60 failures) and later signed in as this user
VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)

actions.action: Immediately disable and force password reset for prof.kaya@aegean.edu; review all sign-ins and enforce MFA/conditional access for the account.
Block IP 193.140.10.21 at perimeter/VPN and review authentication logs for the other sprayed accounts to identify additional successes.
Isolate or urgently patch VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) against CISA KEV CVEs; review VPN logs for anomalous sessions.
Hunt for lateral movement, mailbox rules, and data access tied to the compromised account and VPN appliance.

risk.rationale: Verified password spray by 193.140.10.21 (60 failures across 54 accounts) was followed by a successful sign-in as prof.kaya@aegean.edu, immediately corroborated by impossible travel Manisa→Lisbon in 32 minutes. Together these form a confirmed account takeover chain (credential access via spraying then valid account use from an implausible location). The KEV-listed VPN appliance is an additional exposure to patch/prioritize, but it does not explain away the account compromise. Recommended containment: disable/reset the account, revoke sessions/tokens, force MFA re-enrollment, and investigate the VPN edge appliance.
